overview.text: Dinosaurs (Dinosauria) are a diverse branch of reptiles whose fossils reveal a remarkable range of sizes and forms. They flourished on land during the Mesozoic Era, which includes the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous periods. A key feature distinguishing them from many other reptiles is their upright posture, with legs positioned beneath the body. Some walked on two legs and others on four. Pterosaurs and marine reptiles lived in the same ancient world but were not dinosaurs. Around 66 million years ago, non-bird dinosaurs disappeared in a mass extinction; birds are the surviving dinosaur lineage.

key_facts.text: Non-bird dinosaurs lived during the Mesozoic Era, from roughly 245 to 66 million years ago; its periods are the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous.
Their legs were positioned beneath their bodies; a distinctive hip-socket feature supported this upright stance.
Dinosaurs varied widely in size, and different kinds walked on two or four legs.
Pterosaurs, plesiosaurs, and mosasaurs were prehistoric reptiles, but they were not dinosaurs.
The end-Cretaceous mass extinction about 66 million years ago eliminated non-avian dinosaurs; birds are the surviving dinosaur group.
